notes.title: The ships beyond Brunei: competing voyage sequences
notes.body: Pigafetta dates the foreign fleet's confrontation with junks at Brunei to 29 July 1521 (Robertson's bilingual Ambrosian edition, 1906, vol. XXXIII, pp. 222–225). Albo describes sailing out of the bay; the Genoese pilot's Roteiro instead recounts a re-anchoring, a storm, another capture the following morning, and a two-day wait before leaving (NHCP, Historia Obscura, vol. I, 2025, Document 13, Portuguese pp. 76–79; English pp. 88–90). The Roteiro's calendar dates conflict with Pigafetta's. Ache's question to Ruma about ships 'still outside' is fictional dialogue, not an independently attested sighting or a securely dated fact. These accounts do not establish one reconciled departure time.

notes.title: The missing-person lists are a fictional local response
notes.body: Nasir, his sister, Hasan's inquiry boards, Tahir's questions, the damaged junk's crew and the older woman's search for her son are invented characters and procedures. The narrative deliberately leaves the identities and fates of several missing people unresolved. Pigafetta's report of captured junks does not supply their names or prove what happened to any of these fictional people.

notes.title: Ruma's choices and the proposed northern passage
notes.body: Ruma's upriver trading, her refusal to promise a journey, the uncertain inquiry boat, and the owner who may have room for one passenger are constructed scenes. They show the limits of Ache's knowledge and authority within the story; no cited expedition account records these local negotiations or Ache's exact timetable after his release.
